newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods buy boosts UK market position.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods buy boosts UK market position.

text.p: Littlewoods Organisation's planned acquisition of Freemans may mark the last major restructuring in Britain's stagnant -- but highly profitable -- agency mail order sector, retail experts said on Monday.
Experts said the proposed 395 million pound ($663.8 million) acquisition of the Sears Plc unit would reduce the list of major players in Britain's home shopping market to four.
When the Sears deal is sealed, Littlewoods will remain second in terms of market share after Great Universal Stores Plc (GUS) but the gap between the two will narrow significantly.

"There already has been considerable consolidation. Littlewoods and Freemans were the last two. This is the last piece of the jigsaw, really," said Clive Vaughan, retail consultant at independent consultancy Verdict.

Verdict estimated the size of the British home shopping market at 7.3 billion pounds in 1995, with about 4.3 billion of that coming from agency mail orders and roughly 1.0 billion pounds resulting from direct mail order sales.
The traditional agency mail orders make up most of the market, however, sales in that sector remained little changed from the 4.2 billion chalked up in 1994, Verdict said.
Meanwhile, direct mail order sales rose sharply from 831 million pounds in 1994, a trend that is expected to continue.
Agency mail orders are made via individual agents working on a commission basis whereas mail orders are made directly by customers who select goods from catalogues.
"Agency mail order is growing very, very slowly and probably not at all in real terms, whereas the direct side has grown from very, very small beginnings," Vaughan said.
Experts attributed the decline in the agency mail order business to market saturation and demographic changes.
"A number of working-class women who were previously agents, particularly in the north of England, are literally in a dying market," said Nick Bubb, analyst at Mees Pierson.
"The economics of giving a commission to agents who really only order for themselves, is also a problem," he added, noting that many agents do not have a large list of clients.
Despite the lack of growth in agency mail order sales, the sector still offers strong profits to companies that can compete in the sector.
"Agency mail order is a pretty stable business. It's very cash generative. Once you've covered your fairly high central costs, it is quite a profitable operation," Vaughan said.
He added that Littlewoods seemed to be trying to protect its agency mail order business with the Freemans acquisition.
"It certainly has more of the appearance of being a defensive move (as opposed) to one where any obvious real growth is going to come out," he said.
Littlewoods said the acquisition would increase economies of scale and boost its market share, which will rise to about 23.7 percent from 15.5 percent, according to Verdict figures.

"If you want to have a profitable role in a consolidating industry, then you need to be a very major player. Otherwise you might as well get out, which is presumable what Sears felt about Freemans," Littlewoods chairman James Ross told Reuters.
But retail experts did not expect Littlewoods to overtake market leader GUS, which has a market share of about 24.8 percent, anytime soon.

"GUS are the market leaders and will remain so even after this. They've got plenty of resources to develop, and they will start looking at the next generation of delivering home services using some form of electronic media," Vaughan said.
The following are Britain's top home shopping players, ranked by percentage of market share, according to Verdict:
1) Great Universal Stores 24.8
2) Littlewoods 15.5
3) Freemans 8.2
4) Grattan 7.3
5) Empire 4.0
NOTE: Grattan is owned by Germany's Otto Versand Group, while Empire is part of France's La Redoute. ($1=.5950 Pound)
